{"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-haiku-5-5","id":"msg_011CfzVUpb4RomeKsUFf9g2n","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_011mM94s8z3Cy9Trgx9CFP8H","name":"Edit","input":{"replace_all":false,"file_path":"/home/llmtest/evals/20261012-111947/cholesky_claude-haiku-5.5-cc-medium_omp_r4/cholesky/cholesky.cpp","old_string":"// Simple Cholesky decomposition (sequential, unblocked algorithm)\n// Decomposes positive definite matrix A into L * L^T where L is lower triangular\n\nbool choleskyDecomposition(std::vector<double>& A, const size_t n) {\n    // A is stored in row-major order\n    for (size_t i = 0; i < n; ++i) {\n        for (size_t j = 0; j <= i; ++j) {\n            double sum = 0.0;\n            \n            if (i == j) {\n                // Diagonal element\n                for (size_t k = 0; k < j; ++k) {\n                    sum += A[j * n + k] * A[j * n + k];\n                }\n                const double val = A[j * n + j] - sum;\n                if (val <= 0.0) {\n                    // Matrix is not positive definite\n                    printf(\"Error: Matrix is not positive definite at diagonal element %zu\\n\", j);\n                    return false;\n                }\n                A[j * n + j] = sqrt(val);\n            } else {\n                // Off-diagonal element\n                for (size_t k = 0; k < j; ++k) {\n                    sum += A[i * n + k] * A[j * n + k];\n                }\n                A[i * n + j] = (A[i * n + j] - sum) / A[j * n + j];\n            }\n        }\n        \n        // Zero out upper triangular part\n        for (size_t j = i + 1; j < n; ++j) {\n            A[i * n + j] = 0.0;\n        }\n    }\n    \n    return true;\n}","new_string":"// Cholesky decomposition (OpenMP parallel, unblocked row-wise algorithm)\n// Decomposes positive definite matrix A into L * L^T where L is lower triangular\n\n// Computes row i of L in place. Row i needs the finished diagonal element of every\n// row j < i, so rows run concurrently as a pipeline: row i only waits for the\n// diagonal of the row it is currently reading. Every element is still summed in\n// the same order as the sequential algorithm, so the result is bit-identical.\n// Returns false if this row or an earlier row is not positive definite.\nbool choleskyRow(std::vector<double>& A, const size_t n, const size_t i,\n                 std::vector<std::atomic<bool>>& diagReady,\n                 std::atomic<bool>& failed, std::atomic<size_t>& failedRow) {\n    for (size_t j = 0; j <= i; ++j) {\n        if (j < i) {\n            // Wait until row j is final up to its diagonal (pairs with the release store below)\n            while (!diagReady[j].load(std::memory_order_acquire)) {\n                if (failed.load(std::memory_order_relaxed)) {\n                    return false;\n                }\n                std::this_thread::yield();\n            }\n        }\n\n        double sum = 0.0;\n\n        if (i == j) {\n            // Diagonal element\n            for (size_t k = 0; k < j; ++k) {\n                sum += A[j * n + k] * A[j * n + k];\n            }\n            const double val = A[j * n + j] - sum;\n            if (val <= 0.0) {\n                // Matrix is not positive definite\n                failedRow.store(j);\n                failed.store(true);\n                return false;\n            }\n            A[j * n + j] = sqrt(val);\n            diagReady[j].store(true, std::memory_order_release);\n        } else {\n            // Off-diagonal element\n            for (size_t k = 0; k < j; ++k) {\n                sum += A[i * n + k] * A[j * n + k];\n            }\n            A[i * n + j] = (A[i * n + j] - sum) / A[j * n + j];\n        }\n    }\n\n    // Zero out upper triangular part\n    for (size_t j = i + 1; j < n; ++j) {\n        A[i * n + j] = 0.0;\n    }\n\n    return true;\n}\n\nbool choleskyDecomposition(std::vector<double>& A, const size_t n) {\n    // A is stored in row-major order\n    std::vector<std::atomic<bool>> diagReady(n);\n    std::atomic<bool> failed{false};\n    std::atomic<size_t> failedRow{0};\n\n    // Rows are handed out in increasing order, so every row a thread waits on was\n    // already claimed by a running thread and the pipeline cannot deadlock.\n    // A row only fails after all earlier rows succeeded, so at most one row fails.\n    #pragma omp parallel for schedule(dynamic, 1)\n    for (size_t i = 0; i < n; ++i) {\n        choleskyRow(A, n, i, diagReady, failed, failedRow);\n    }\n\n    if (failed.load()) {\n        printf(\"Error: Matrix is not positive definite at diagonal element %zu\\n\", failedRow.load());\n        return false;\n    }\n\n    return true;\n}"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"container":null,"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":14064,"cache_read_input_tokens":17591,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":14064},"output_tokens":8,"service_tier":"standard","inference_geo":"not_available"},"input_transformations":[],"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"214ebda5-fce6-4860-bec3-1e0d161eaa49","uuid":"4441a926-839f-4342-b233-361d90b97598","timestamp":"2026-10-13T15:42:52.023Z","request_id":"req_011CfzVUpBFwrCAa7ud59iiM"}

The output matches the original bit-for-bit, and the decomposition runs about 59× faster at n=2048 on 64 threads.\n\n**Changes (existing files only; executable is still `cholesky`):**\n\n- **`cholesky/cholesky.cpp`**\n  - **Decomposition:** rows run concurrently as a pipeline. Row `i` only waits for the diagonal element of each earlier row `j` it reads, which is published with a release/acquire atomic flag. Summation order per element is unchanged, so results are identical to the sequential version.\n  - **Failure path:** a non-positive-definite diagonal sets a shared flag. Waiting rows see it and exit instead of hanging, and the same error message is printed for the same index as before.\n  - **Matrix generation** (`B·Bᵀ`) and **validation** (`L·Lᵀ` and the error max-reduction) are parallel loops. The random-number fill stays sequential so the generated matrix is unchanged.\n- **`cholesky/CMakeLists.txt`:** `find_package(OpenMP REQUIRED)` and link `OpenMP::OpenMP_CXX`. OpenMP is unconditional, and there are no new external dependencies.\n\n**Verification:**\n- Original and new builds were compared across n = 1, 2, 3, 17, 64, 255, 512, 1000 with `-v -r`. The printed results, hashes, and validation output are identical, excluding timing lines.\n- The non-positive-definite path was tested with a scratch harness in `/tmp` (not in the project). It reports the failure and does not hang across repeated runs.\n\n**Timing (decomposition only, ms):**\n\n| n | original | 1 thr | 8 thr | 64 thr |\n|---|---|---|---|---|\n| 512 | 28 | 30 | 4 | 2 |\n| 2048 | 2134 | 2149 | 280 | 36 |\n\nSpeedup is close to linear through 64 threads at n=2048.\n\n**Choices I made:**\n- I kept the exact floating-point operation order instead of using multiple accumulators in the dot products. That would vectorize better but would change rounding, so I didn't do it.\n- I didn't add a thread-count line to the output, to keep the output format unchanged.\n- `output.txt` and `common/` are untouched.
